name: The Tome of Divinity

angles.text: A paladin faces this trial through selfless aid to the innocent, not steel or combat. Such compassion is a virtue at the heart of the Holy Light.
For the Alliance, this reveals the Scourge's deep wounds in human homes and the reliance between Stormwind and Ironforge.

faq.answer: John Turner is a human caretaker who runs a Stormwind orphanage with his wife. About once a month, he travels to Ironforge to seek supplies and charity from dwarven citizens and merchant guilds for children orphaned by war.

aliases: why does john turner need cloth
faq.answer: John Turner needs linen cloth so his wife in Stormwind can sew warm clothes for the orphaned children. More tradesmen across Azeroth and shifting trade have made basic cloth scarce and hard to find.
faq.q: Why does John Turner need linen cloth?

faq.answer: The children in the Turners' care lost their parents in the Scourge's devastating assaults over the past decade. The Third War shattered families across the human kingdoms and left many young people without homes.
faq.q: Why are there so many orphans in Stormwind?

aliases: why is john turner in ironforge
faq.answer: John Turner travels across the mountains to Ironforge to ask dwarven citizens and trade groups for donations and supplies that are hard to find in Stormwind.
faq.q: Why did John Turner travel to Ironforge?

aliases: what does this have to do with the light
why do paladins do this quest
faq.answer: The Holy Light calls for selflessness, mercy, and service to those in despair. Helping a weary caretaker provide for war orphans tests an aspiring paladin's humility and charity.
faq.q: How does helping an orphanage relate to the Holy Light?

faq.answer: John Turner's trip has been slow and unproductive because supplies are scarce and few groups have offered help. He cannot return home until he secures a shipment.
faq.q: Why has John Turner's trip to Ironforge been so difficult?

sections.body: For an initiate walking the path of the Light, the trial in Ironforge calls for charity rather than arms. John Turner has come to the dwarven halls seeking help. He and his wife oversee an orphanage in Stormwind, where they care for children left without parents by the Scourge's rampages over the past decade. His journey to Ironforge speaks to the hardships shared by the Alliance's common folk.
sections.title: Charity in the Great Forge

sections.body: Provisions are hard to gather across borders. More tradesmen have come to work across Azeroth, and local supplies have grown scarce. John Turner has spent weeks in Ironforge appealing to civic groups and citizens, with little to show for it. His wife needs linen cloth to make clothes for the children. Giving it freely shows the selfless devotion at the heart of a servant of the Light.
sections.title: The Scars of the Scourge

summary: In Ironforge, The Tome of Divinity calls servants of the Light to show compassion. John Turner seeks aid for the Stormwind orphanage he runs with his wife, caring for children left parentless by the Scourge. The trial asks an initiate to choose charity over martial glory.
attribution: In-game quest text: The Tome of Divinity
